physical.title: box; pail
physical.summary: A Micmac birchbark container (mocock) with etched linear design, wide and rectangular at the base with a smaller, circular opening at the top. The sides are joined by inverted Y seams stitched with plant fibre cord (spruce root?), that is also wrapped around the rim of the opening. There was likely once a plant fibre strap, although now there are only fragments of such a strap at opposite sides of the top opening. There is extensive discolouring inside the box, indicating historic use (maple syrup?). The base of the box has a number of small cracks and one significant break running from front to back.

physical.title: box
physical.summary: A circular Micmac etched birchbark box and lid, with sides made from birchbark and a wooden (cedar?) lid and base. The seam is stitched with plant fibre (reed?) and reinforced with wooden pegs, which are also used to attach the base and lid top to the birch bark sides. These areas are also reinforced with metal nails, unevenly spaced around the circumference. The sides of the box have etched decoration with a series of repeating geometric designs resembling an eight pointed asterisk, while the lid is decorated with a vertical zig-zag pattern.
